title: Interlock Logic & Cause Effect Matrix - CT-7801 (SEQ-7801)
content:
INTERLOCK LOGIC & CAUSE EFFECT MATRIX: SEQ-7801 (COOLING TOWER FAN (CT-7801) SHUTDOWN LOGIC).
Document No: TJC-LLD-IL-CT-7801, Revision: Rev.03, Status: Issued for Operation, SIL Level: SIL 1.
Equipment: CT-7801, Functional Location: TJC-LLD-7800-01.
CAUSE & EFFECT MATRIX (TRIPS):
- T1: Fan/gearbox vibration HIGH-HIGH (VSHH-7802 > 9 mm/s, 1oo1) -> Actions: Trip Motor (EFF-1), DCS Alarm (EFF-2), Start Standby Pump STANDBY (EFF-3)
- T2: Gearbox oil temperature HIGH-HIGH (TSHH-7803 > 90 degC, 1oo1) -> Actions: Trip Motor (EFF-1), DCS Alarm (EFF-2), Start Standby Pump STANDBY (EFF-3)
- T3: Gearbox oil pressure LOW (PSL-7807 < 0.8 barg, 1oo1) -> Actions: Trip Motor (EFF-1), DCS Alarm (EFF-2)
- T4: Fan motor overload (MPR-7801 MPR pickup, 1oo1) -> Actions: Trip Motor (EFF-1), DCS Alarm (EFF-2), Start Standby Pump STANDBY (EFF-3)
START PERMISSIVES (AND-gate conditions to start):
- P1: Gearbox oil level OK (LG gearbox, Gate: AND)
- P2: Basin level normal (> LSL-7804) (LT-7804, Gate: AND)
- P3: No fan lockout / maintenance key released (lockout, Gate: AND)
- —: ALL permissives TRUE → START CT-7801 ENABLED (—, Gate: AND)
CROSS REFERENCES: P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-7801, Datasheet: TJC-LLD-DS-CT-7801.

title: One Point Lesson - Barscreen Cleaning (Suction Screen) (OPL-CT-7801-01)
content:

References: Interlock: SEQ-7801 (SIL 1), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-7801.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains barscreen cleaning (suction screen) for CT-7801 (COOLING TOWER CELL FAN) in the COOLING TOWER SYSTEM. A clogged barscreen starves the circulating water pumps and fouls the fill, reducing cooling for the whole unit. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

- Precaution 5: Have emergency actions and communications ready before starting.

- Tool 3: Gas detector (O2 / LEL) as required
- Tool 4: Correct PPE for the fluid handled
- Tool 5: Sample containers & PPE for sampling
- Tool 6: Permit-to-work documentation

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Rake the SS304 barscreen every shift on the round
- Step 1 - Check: Permit valid & briefed
- Step 2 - Action: Remove leaves, debris and biological growth
- Step 2 - Check: Parameter within limit
- Step 3 - Action: Check the differential level across the screen
- Step 3 - Check: Interlock status confirmed
- Step 4 - Action: Dispose of debris correctly and log the cleaning
- Step 4 - Check: Change logged on DCS

- Step 5 - Check: Handover to next shift

- Symptom: VSHH-7802 vibration alarm on CT-7801 fan | Cause: Leading-edge erosion on one FRP blade caused imbalance | Action: Inspected blades, re-balanced fan, vibration normalised

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: A clogged barscreen starves the circulating water pumps and fouls the fill, reducing cooling for the whole unit.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-7801: e.g. VSHH-7802 trips at > 9 mm/s - never defeat it without a permit.
